# Changelog

All notable changes to Sando UI are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this
project follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html): while the major version
is 0, a breaking change bumps the minor version and every other change the patch version. Between
releases the version is the next release's `-dev` prerelease (`0.2.0-dev` before `0.2.0`). The
version a copy of this file describes is in the `VERSION` file the `guide` item installs beside it
(`docs/sando/VERSION`).

Every entry that needs your edit opens with `**Breaking:**`, so `grep -n 'Breaking:'` lists them all.

## [Unreleased]

## [0.1.0] - 2026-11-10

### Added

- **The version reaches your repository**: the `guide` item now installs `docs/sando/VERSION`
  (the Sando version you installed) and `docs/sando/CHANGELOG.md` (this file), so after a re-sync
  `git diff docs/sando/CHANGELOG.md` shows exactly what changed since your last install. Every
  registry item also carries `meta.sandoVersion`, which `npx shadcn view` prints.
- **Versioned registry addresses**: each release is served at `/r/<version>/{name}.json` and never
  changes, beside `/r/latest/` (the newest release) and `/r/next/` (unreleased work). Point the
  `@sando-ui` entry of your `components.json` at one version, so every `add` and re-sync installs
  that version until you move it on purpose. The public host is `https://sando-ui.github.io`.
- **Brands**: `lychee` (an achromatic brand with a blue accent, item `brand-lychee`), and a
  `brand-avocado` item now that avocado is no longer the default (see Changed).
- **Layouts**: `Show` (shows its children from or below a breakpoint step), `Indent`, `Layer`;
  `Stack` `grow`; `Grid` `itemWidth`; `LayoutGrid` `padding` and `rowGap`; `Container` `span` and
  `align` (see Changed).
- **Components**: `Text` (a type role as a unit: `variant`, `size`, `isEmphasized`, `tone` of
  `default` / `muted` / `emphasis` / `urgency`, `maxLines`), `Band`, `Media`, `Rating`, `PinField`,
  `FieldButton`, `LinkButton`, `ResizeHandle`, `SpacingField`, `Countdown`, `StickyBar`,
  `DockedBar`, `StepLadder`, `SiteHeader`.
- **Blocks**: `SidePanel`, `PlanCard`, `PlanCardCompact`, `PriceSummary`, `PriceComparison`,
  `DealCard`, `QuickFilterRail`, `RangeFilterSheet`, `OptionSheet`,
  `ListControls`, `ReviewForm`, `SocialLogin`, `BottomNavDocked`.
- **PlanCard and PlanCardCompact `headingLevel`** (optional, default `3`, today's output): pass `2`
  when a plan list sits directly under the page's h1, so the heading outline skips no level.
- **Shared modules** pulled in by the units that need them: `icons` (see Changed), `control-size`,
  `resolve-offset`, `use-scroll-clearance`.
- **Five control sizes**: `x-small` and `x-large` join `small` / `medium` / `large` on Button and
  the other sized controls (NumberField stops at `small`, its steppers do not fit 24px).
- **New props and variants** (all optional): AppShell `variant="inset"`, `rail`, `bottomNav`,
  `bottomBar`, `breakpoint`; Navbar `brandCompact`, `utilityLinks`, `search`, `isSticky`,
  `breakpoint`; Card `isFeatured`, `CardRibbon`, `CardActionArea`, `CardMedia`, CardFooter
  `isFlush`; Badge `size`, `category` (1 to 8) and the status tints `success` / `warning` /
  `info`; ListBox and GridList `variant` (GridList `contained`, ListBox grid layout), `indicator`,
  `renderEmptyState`, item `media` / `trailing` / `unavailableLabel`; Select and ComboBox
  `labelPlacement="inside"`, ComboBox `leading`, Select and Menu item `trailing`; Switch and Slider
  `thumbShape`, Slider `isInset`; Switch `labelPlacement`; CheckboxGroup and RadioGroup `variant`
  (`filled`); Carousel `indicator` (`counter`) and `controlsFrom`; Collapsible `triggerVariant`,
  `chevronPlacement`; ContextualHelp, ProgressBar, SubNav, NavigationRail and NavItem `size`;
  DrawerForm `variant`, `responsive`, `onReset`; Breadcrumb item `onPress`; Table column and cell
  `align`; Wizard `stepIndex` / `onStepChange`; DescriptionList takes a node as a term; Tooltip
  `offset`; Separator and ToolbarSeparator `isDecorative`.
- **Sys roles**: `urgency` (`--sd-color-text-urgency`, `--sd-color-fill-urgency-subtle`) beside
  `emphasis`; per-tier surface inner radius `--sd-surface-radius-inner-<tier>`.
- **The consumer guide installs with `styles`.** Every install now writes Sando's guide to
  `docs/sando/*.md` (new item `guide`, a dependency of `styles`): installing, theming, the rules for
  your own CSS and compositions, and which unit to use. Point your coding agent at it with the
  snippet in `docs/sando/getting-started.md` § For your coding agent.
- **A standard layout for a product's repository.** `docs/sando/design-language.md` now defines
  where a product keeps its design (`design/DESIGN.md`, `design/SCREENS.md`, `design/product.json`),
  the `sando:install` script that installs the theme and every unit `product.json` lists, where
  screens go (`src/screens/`), and the order an agent reads these in to build a screen, with a
  template for `SCREENS.md` (its § Flows is where flows between screens live) and the `product.json`
  fields. The `DESIGN.md` template now separates the shared UX principles (a pointer to this guide)
  from the service's own UX policy, and § A finding becomes a rule says how a review's defect is
  sent upstream as a `[finding]` issue or recorded in `design/`. The agent snippet in
  `docs/sando/getting-started.md` § For your coding agent states that order; paste it again.
- **Two npm packages for the tools: `@sando-ui/cli` (the `sando` command) and
  `@sando-ui/eslint-plugin`.** Units stay copied into your repository; the tools that install and
  check them are devDependencies at the exact Sando version, released under the same number
  (`docs/sando/getting-started.md` § Install the tools). `sando install` installs the brand and every
  unit in `design/product.json` at the recorded version, pins the `@sando-ui` address in
  `components.json` to `/r/<version>/`, stops before overwriting an installed file you changed, and
  writes `design/sando.lock.json` and the `sando` key of `product.json`. `sando check` runs the static
  checks and the ESLint rules (screen purity, installed units only, `policy`, your own CSS), with an
  adoption baseline in `design/sando-baseline.json` that only falls. `sando verify` renders every
  screen in every story, width, scheme, theme and context and judges the renders (errors, axe,
  overflow, primary buttons per viewport). `sando review <Name>` is a report-only AI design review
  that also drafts a `[finding]` issue body. All four, and how to adopt them in an existing
  repository, are `docs/sando/getting-started.md` § Checking your repository.
- **`design/product.json` fields**: `prefix` (your own class prefix), `theme` as a list of brands
  (each rendered by `sando verify`), `policy` (the checkable part of your UX policy: unit limits per
  screen type, allowed prop values by position, the primary-button budget, the imports a screen may
  not use, the render time zone) and `sando` (written by `sando install`). The schema ships in
  `@sando-ui/cli` at `schema/product.schema.json`.
- **The tools, from the telecom-web adoption.** `policy.render.schemes` limits the colour schemes
  `sando verify` renders (default both; `["light"]` for a product with no dark mode), and
  `policy.screenTypes.<type>.budgets` overrides `policy.budgets` for the screens of that type.
  `sando verify --set-baseline` and `--baseline-prune` keep an adoption baseline of its own in
  `design/sando-verify-baseline.json` (one count per failing render, per rule and screen file; it
  only falls, and R3 is never baselined), so a service can adopt `sando verify` before an upstream
  fix lands. `sando install` now prints the global sheets to import after it installs, and
  `--version 0.1.0-dev` (a prerelease number) reads `/r/next/` as `--version next` does.
- **`policy.render.pages`**: the HTML pages whose `<html>` `sando verify` R3 reads for `lang` and
  `data-brand`, as paths from your repository root (`["dist/index.html"]`). Until now R3 read only a
  root `index.html`, so a repository whose build scripts write its pages could never pass. Absent, R3
  reads `index.html` as before; listed, each page must exist (build before `sando verify`) and carry
  both attributes (`docs/sando/design-language.md` § design/product.json).
- **Fixed in the tools.** `sando check` no longer crashes in a repository on TypeScript 7 (the
  plugin keeps its parser on the TypeScript 6 it brings), so no `overrides` entry is needed: drop the
  `ts-api-utils` override if you added one. Installed Sando files (`src/components`, `src/blocks`,
  `src/layouts`, `src/styles`) are no longer linted at all, so a disable comment in one of them for
  a rule the shared config does not register (`icons.tsx`, `Toast.tsx`) is no longer an error;
  remove any baseline entry you wrote for it. S2 reads only `## <N>. <ScreenName>` headings (N from
  1, at most one parenthetical after the name) as screen entries, and S4 the `### N.3` part. R8
  counts only the topmost layer: a primary button behind an open modal dialog, or under `inert` or
  `aria-hidden`, no longer counts. `screenTypes` limits now reach units a screen places through a
  `src/screens/lib/` module it imports. U8 says no release is published yet when `/r/latest/` serves
  nothing. A missing browser names the driver's own install command, `npx playwright-core install
  chromium`. `sando verify` blocks every request leaving the harness before the page loads and waits
  for every font face visible text uses, so two runs render the same bytes; serve fonts from your
  repository, since a web font from a CDN never paints in the renders.
- **Guide: what the checks read, stated exactly.** `docs/sando/composition-contract.md` § Accessibility
  you owe now says every screen has exactly one `h1`, visually hidden with `sd-visually-hidden` when
  the design shows no title, which `sando verify` already blocked on. `docs/sando/design-language.md`
  says `units` lists every unit a file under `src/screens/` imports, even one another listed unit
  brings, and how to derive it; gives the `DESIGN.md` outline at its heading levels (`## Part 1`,
  `## Part 2`, numbered `###` sections inside Part 2); and gives the `SCREENS.md` grammar: a screen
  entry is `## N. <Name>` named after its file, `## Conventions` and `## Flows` are unnumbered, and
  the five parts are `### N.1` to `### N.5`. If you copied the earlier template, unnumber
  `## 0. Conventions`. `docs/sando/getting-started.md` adds the `eslint.config.js` a service writes,
  where to keep the tarballs before the packages are published (`vendor/sando-ui/`), what
  `/r/latest/` and `/r/next/` serve and what `--version` takes, and installs the browser with
  `npx playwright-core install chromium` so it matches the CLI's driver.
- **Screens and service logic** (`docs/sando/design-language.md`): a screen renders from its props
  alone, with fetching, storage, URL state, the clock and effects in a route layer (`src/app/` by
  default, a table for other frameworks); each screen's states are CSF3 stories in
  `src/screens/<Name>.stories.tsx`, named after its `SCREENS.md` N.3; and § The layout now lists
  `design/sando.lock.json`, `design/sando-baseline.json`, `src/app/`, `src/assets/` and `.sando/`.

- Alert (and Banner) `neutral` variant, a note with no judgement, and Separator `variant="band"`, a
  thick neutral strip between page sections.
- ProductTile `zone` (1 to 8): the owner's colour as a categorical palette slot fills the whole tile
  with on-colour ink; `swatch` stays the edge for any other colour.
- ToggleButtonGroup `secondary` selects in `fill.neutral.strong` with its own ink, and
  `fill.neutral.strong` now keeps 3:1 from the neutral fill at rest, so selection never rests on hue.
- Button `tonal` (medium emphasis on the brand's tint) and `strong` (the neutral solid co-equal with
  `primary`) variants (ADR-0046).
- `color.config.json § secondary.treatment` and the Sys roles `fill.secondary` / `border.secondary`:
  a brand decides whether the ladder's non-primary Button is filled or outlined (ADR-0045).
- `contrast.onColorDestructive`: the destructive fill's own on-colour floor, so a brand can lower
  its primary's floor and still keep white on red (ADR-0021 Amendment 1).
- Project governance & documentation: `LICENSE` (MIT), `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, rewritten
  `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, `SECURITY.md`.
- Architecture Decision Record log under `docs/decisions/` (ADR-0001: documentation and
  governance structure) with a reusable MADR template.
- `docs/prior-art.md` — borrow / concept / reject narrative and design-token authorities.
- **DTCG token pipeline (Phase 1)**: DTCG JSON token source under `tokens/` (`ref`/`sys`/`cmp`),
  with `src/styles/tokens.css` now **generated** by Style Dictionary via a custom `sando/css`
  format (`npm run token:build`). Typography is a `$type: typography` composite; theme/responsive
  variants ride in `$extensions.sando.*`. Verified at 0-diff parity with the prior hand-authored CSS.
  ADR-0003; `docs/prior-art.md` moves DTCG/Style Dictionary from REJECT to BORROW. The source is
  platform-neutral, keeping native (iOS/Android) + Figma outputs possible as a future phase.
- **Typography as utility classes + line-height system** (ADR-0004): `.sd-type-<role>` classes are
  generated from the DTCG `typography` composites; components apply a type role as one class instead
  of per-property font tokens (resolves the fragmented consumption; ~200 Cmp type tokens removed).
  New Sys `--sd-line-height-{none,tight,normal,relaxed}` scale; 22 line-height literals tokenized;
  `label` role line-heights retuned 1.4→1.25 for compact UI. Size-variant text and icon glyphs are
  documented exceptions. `.claude/rules/` updated (component-contract §6/§7, naming-convention
  § Typography / § Literals).

- **Motion duration scale consolidated**: component `*-animation-duration` literals (17, raw ms/s)
  rewired to a Sys scale — `--sd-duration-fast(120)/moderate(160)/slow(240)` for transitions/entrances
  plus `spin(720)/pulse(1200)/slide(1100)/reduced(1500)` for looping/reduced-motion. `fast`/`moderate`
  retuned (100→120, 180→160) to match real usage. No raw duration literals remain in tokens.

- **`src/styles/token-names.json`** in the `styles` item: the Sys and Cmp custom property names and
  the shared public classes your stylesheets may use, generated from the shipped stylesheets. The
  `@sando-ui/eslint-plugin` CSS and className rules read it; you never edit it, and a re-sync
  replaces it.

### Changed

- **A heading level is typed `1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6`.** `headingLevel` on `AccordionItem`, `CardTitle`,
  `PlanCard`, `PlanCardCompact` and `SidePanel` took any `number`, so `7` rendered an `<h7>`. Nothing renders
  differently; a call site passing a number outside 1 to 6 now fails to type-check. `CardTitle`
  documents its default, `3`, which it already had.
- **Install with `sando install`, not the `npx shadcn` script.** The `sando:install` script that
  `docs/sando/design-language.md` gave you is replaced: set `"sando:install": "sando install"` in
  `package.json`
  and run `sando install --version <version>` once to record your version
  (`docs/sando/getting-started.md` § Install units). § Upgrading is now: move both packages to the
  new version, `sando install --version <new>`, read `git diff docs/sando/CHANGELOG.md`, then
  `sando:check -- --all`. The agent snippet in § For your coding agent now has the agent keep
  screens pure and run `sando:check` and look at the screenshots before it calls a screen finished;
  paste it again.
- **Breaking:** **the default brand is mango, not avocado.** The `styles` item now ships
  `src/styles/themes/mango.css`, which claims plain `:root`; `avocado.css` is no longer part of
  `styles` and now paints only under `data-brand="avocado"` on `<html>`. A re-sync no longer
  brings or updates `avocado.css`, and the regenerated file paints nothing without that attribute.
  To stay on avocado: add `brand-avocado` and set `<html data-brand="avocado">`. To move to mango:
  replace your `avocado.css` import with `mango.css` (or with `styles` alone) and delete
  `avocado.css`. Mango itself was retuned (orange `#FF9E20` on white, squircle corners, Pretendard
  text at a 16px base), so pixels move either way.
- **Breaking:** **icons come from `lucide-react` through a new `icons` module.** Units no longer import
  `reicon-react`; they import glyphs from `src/components/icons.tsx` (item `icons`, which also
  ships `src/styles/icons.css`, which `icons.tsx` imports itself). Re-adding any unit pulls
  `icons`; run `npm i lucide-react` and drop `reicon-react` once nothing of yours uses it.
- **Breaking:** **Badge `strong` is renamed `tonal`** (the brand tint). `strong` now draws the dark
  neutral solid that Button's `strong` uses. Replace `variant="strong"` with `variant="tonal"` to
  keep the look.
- **Breaking:** **AppShell moved from `src/layouts/` to `src/components/`** (it paints a surface, so it
  is a Component). Update imports to `components/AppShell` and delete the old two files.
- **Breaking:** **Container's `size` is gone.** A Container now spans columns of the large page grid:
  `span` (6, 8, 12 or `"full"`, default 12), `align` (`center` or `start`), and `padding`, which
  is `"page"` (default) or `"none"`. Below the large step every span is the whole grid. Map `small`
  / `medium` / `large` to a span.
- **Breaking:** **the neutral Ref ramp is `--sd-ref-palette-gray-*`, not `cool-gray-*`**, in every
  brand, with identical values. Other Ref rungs are named by their value, so the retunes above also
  renamed a few `--sd-ref-font-size-*`, `-line-height-*`, `-size-*`, `-radius-*` and `-space-*`
  rungs. If your CSS reads Sys roles (`--sd-color-*`, `--sd-space-*`) no edit is needed; a direct
  Ref read must be repointed, or it goes invalid and unsets the property.
- **Breaking:** **control radius follows control size.** `--sd-radius-control` is replaced by
  `--sd-radius-control-{x-small,small,medium,large,x-large}`.
- **Breaking:** **58 component custom properties in `tokens.css` were split or retired**, mostly per
  size or per part: `--sd-button-radius` and `--sd-select-trigger-radius` became
  `...-radius-<size>`, `--sd-tabs-tab-padding-inline-small` became
  `--sd-tabs-tab-padding-inline-contained-<size>`, and the text padding properties
  (`--sd-dialog-body-text-padding-inline`, `--sd-popover-content-text-padding-*`, and similar) are
  gone because text takes the shared text inset (next entry). If your own CSS overrides a
  `--sd-<component>-*` property, check it still exists in the new `tokens.css`.
- **Every `.sd-type-*` text stands one text inset in**, padded on both inline sides by the brand's
  `--sd-text-inset-inline`, and `reset.css` zeroes it for inline runs inside a sentence. Markup of
  your own that uses those classes shifts inward by that inset. With it, 37 `*-text` and `__label`
  style part classes are no longer styled (for example `.sd-card__content-text`,
  `.sd-dialog__body-text`, `.sd-cartsummary__total-label`); CSS of yours aimed at one stops
  matching.
- ConsentChecklist's `terms`, `submitLabel` and `onSubmit` are optional now that `groups` exists.
- Brand values moved without renames (they change pixels, not names): aronia retuned to a blue on a
  cool grey paper, blueberry and mango warnings moved off their accents, and a checkbox's or switch's
  control-to-label gap grew one rung.

- **Breaking:** `ConfirmDialog` renders at `width="small"` (the brand's `overlay.width.small`, 288/384, aronia 320/384), not the 480 `medium` default; `Dialog` gains `x-large` and `2x-large` widths. OrderLine's stepper widens with its control height (three heights, floored at 8rem), so `size="large"` grows from 128 to 144.
- **Breaking:** the ladder's non-primary Button is `secondary`, not `outline` (ADR-0045). In an outline
  brand it looks as before; `ConfirmDialog`'s `confirmVariant` takes `"secondary"` where it took
  `"outline"`, and `outline` is now the media look only.
- **Breaking:** **for anyone who has vendored a theme file, the Ref vivid colour rungs are gone,
  and every fill colour moved a little.** `--sd-ref-palette-<hue>-solid` and `-solid-strong` no longer
  exist and nothing replaces them. A fill role now picks one of the ramp's 21 rungs instead of
  minting a step of its own, so `--sd-color-fill-error` reads `--sd-ref-palette-red-500` where it
  used to read `red-solid`. **The palette is now exactly 21 rungs per hue with no exceptions**: 20
  Ref colours were deleted and none added.
  All 21 fill values across the three brands shift by less than one rung of the ramp (under 4.85 L\*),
  no fill's ink flips, and every WCAG pairing still passes. The largest single move is a brand fill:
  avocado `#42642B` → `#3D5D27`. A consumer who took `src/styles/themes/<brand>.css` whole and reads
  Sys roles (`--sd-color-fill-brand` and its siblings) needs no edit but will see the new colours; a
  consumer whose own CSS reads a `-solid` / `-solid-strong` custom property directly must repoint it
  to a rung, and an unrepointed reference goes invalid-at-computed-value-time, which unsets the
  property rather than falling back.
  `contrast.onColor`, the ink floor a status fill must clear, went from 4.5 (bare WCAG AA) to **5**
  in the same pass, which moves `fill.error` one rung lighter again and takes its label from 4.57 to
  5.42. It is the only role the change touches in any brand.
  The reasoning, every moved value, and what it cost is ADR-0038 in the Sando repository. It
  supersedes ADR-0037, which the same day had
  renamed those rungs to their ramp position (`red-474`, `red-619`) before the rung itself was
  removed. Neither name was ever served by a registry host, which is why the break is spent now.

- **Block tier consolidation (redundancy prune)** — merged two redundant Blocks into their
  canonical siblings. `DangerZone` now composes `ConfirmDialog` (with `confirmVariant="secondary"`,
  preserving its prior look) instead of the separate `AlertDialog`; the checkout example moved to a
  `CheckoutFlow` story on `Wizard`. Block count 93 → 91. (Registry regeneration deferred to commit.)

### Removed

- **Breaking:** **the `internet-offer-card` item (InternetOfferCard Block).** It served one service's
  page and no other. If you installed it, keep `src/blocks/InternetOfferCard.{tsx,css}` as your own
  local unit (a re-sync no longer updates it), or compose the offer from `Card`, `Badge` and
  `Accordion`.
- **Breaking:** **the product presets `product-telecom` and `product-studio`.** Sando no longer ships a
  product: your product's choices, its `DESIGN.md` and its screens live in your own repository
  (`docs/sando/design-language.md` is the template). If you installed one, keep the files it wrote
  under `products/<name>/` as your own, and install the brand it used with `add @sando-ui/brand-<name>`
  (or `styles` for the default brand); the units it brought stay installed and keep updating
  item by item.
- **Breaking:** **the `collapsible-rail` item (CollapsibleRail Block).** Use `side-panel`, or put the
  rail in AppShell's `rail` slot. Delete `src/blocks/CollapsibleRail.{tsx,css}` after the re-sync.
- **Breaking:** **`--sd-container-{small,medium,large}` and `--sd-overlay-margin-large`**, with no
  replacement: a container's width is now a grid span, and a side drawer's keep-out floor is
  `--sd-overlay-margin-medium`.
- **Breaking:** **ToolbarSeparator's `variant`** (it drew nothing); drop the prop.
- Chart no longer emits `data-type` and DescriptionList no longer emits `data-orientation`; neither
  was styled, but a selector of yours that read one stops matching.

- **`AlertDialog` Block** — folded into `ConfirmDialog` (a near-identical superset). A Button
  `destructive` variant is still not implemented, so destructive confirms use `secondary` for now.
- **`CheckoutStepper` Block** — a thin preset over `Wizard`; demoted to a `Wizard` story
  (`CheckoutFlow`).

### Fixed

- **`--sd-color-focus-ring` was undefined** — components referenced it for focus outlines but no
  Sys token existed (predated the DTCG work). Added `color.focus-ring` (theme-varying: blue-600
  light / blue-400 dark, matching `border.focus`). No dangling token references remain repo-wide.
- **BottomActionBar is a region landmark.** The row renders `role="region"` named by its required
  `aria-label` (it was `role="group"`), so a bar docked in AppShell's `bottomBar` or `bottomNav`
  outside `main` is no longer content outside every landmark. Drop a `role="region"` you added to
  the `DockedBar` around it, or the bar is announced as two regions.
- **DealCard's link is named by its content.** It carried `aria-label={title}`, which left the
  discount and prices out of the name (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name). The name is now the card's text
  (the picture's `alt`, then title, discount and prices); nothing to change at the call site.
- **DealCard's title no longer cuts mid-word in a narrow column.** The title and discount row
  now wraps, so when both do not fit side by side the discount drops under the title and the title
  keeps the full width for its two lines; nothing to change at the call site.
- **`sando verify` R4 sees a focus ring painted on a part.** It compared only the focused element's
  own outline and box-shadow, so a vertical `Button` (its ring is on the round plate) read as
  showing no focus. R4 now compares the outline, box-shadow and border of the focused element, its
  descendants and their `::before`/`::after` against their unfocused look; an element whose look
  does not change on focus is reported, even one with a permanent shadow.
- **`sando review` says the UX principles are not installed yet.** No item ships
  `docs/sando/ux-principles.md` while the principles await approval; the report and the console line
  now say so and name the criteria judged from the spec alone without them (D1, D2, D3, D5, D6, D7,
  D8). Once approved they ship in the `guide` item.
- **A `SCREENS.md` entry written with bold parts is reported, not read as empty.** An entry whose
  parts were bold text (`**1.3 States**`) instead of `### 1.3` headings gave S4 and R7 nothing to

This file answers exactly one question: **when the library offers several components for the same need, what decides between them?** No single component file can hold that answer: whichever `.tsx` you wrote it in, the other one would be missing it. **What this file is not.** It does not state prop defaults or when to deviate from one: each prop's own doc comment owns that, and `@default` records it. It does not list what a Block composes, and nothing does today. It does not decide which tier a unit belongs to or how tiers compose; that is [`composition-contract.md`](composition-contract.md). It does not assign type roles; [`styling-contract.md`](styling-contract.md) does, and several entries below simply carry that ruling's consequence. Which `size` and `variant` to pass is [`prop-usage-contract.md`](prop-usage-contract.md). ## How to read an entry Each entry names the fork, gives the criterion, and marks how far the criterion is enforced: - **L2**: Sando's own build fails when its code breaks the rule, and some of these are also pinned in the types you installed. Treat it as fixed in your code too, even where nothing in your repository checks it. - **L0**: prose. A judgment call, and deviating is allowed when the case warrants it. An agent composing a screen should read the marker before deciding it knows better. --- ## Picking one thing out of a set **Select · ComboBox · Autocomplete · ListBox · Menu**: five ways to offer a set, split by two questions: *does the user pick a value, or run a command?* and *does the set need filtering?* | Reach for | When | L | |---|---|---| | `Select` | a value is chosen from a short, fixed set, and the chosen value stays visible in a trigger. `selectionMode="multiple"` picks several, listed in the trigger, each option then carrying a check; for several picks that should all stay visible as chips, use `TagGroup` | L0 | | `ComboBox` | the same, but the set is long enough that typing to narrow it is faster than scrolling, or the user may enter a value not in the list. `selectionMode="multiple"` picks several as `Select` does: the input stays a search and a line under the field lists the choices | L0 | | `ListBox` | the set is always visible; there is no trigger and nothing to open | L0 | | `Menu` | the items are **commands** that do something, not values that get stored | L0 | | `Autocomplete` | you are building a command palette. A prose scope needs them by construction: it styles a document, which is what `@tailwindcss/typography`'s `prose` does, and Sando is Vanilla CSS, not Tailwind, by a settled decision. So it is not a component to add, it is a model to change. **What would change the answer** is a real article or blog screen. If you are building one before Sando ships a prose scope, it is yours to build under your own prefix ([`missing-units.md`](missing-units.md)). ## When a field takes a placeholder **A field takes a `placeholder` only when it has NO visible label, or when the placeholder carries an example or format the label cannot.** Never as a restatement of the label: a placeholder disappears the moment someone types, so anything essential must survive in the label or `description`. Most fields have a visible label and need no hint, which is why most Sando inputs render empty. The Blocks that do pass one fall into three shapes: | Shape | Call sites | |---|---| | no visible label, so the placeholder is the only hint | ChatWindow · CommandMenu · CommentThread · DataTable · NewsletterSignup | | the placeholder comes from a prop, so the consumer decides | FilterBar · MultiSelectList · SearchBar · SearchList | | a visible label **plus** an example value the label cannot carry | ApiKeyManager (`"Production deployment"` under `Key label`) | The shape to avoid is a label repeating the format the placeholder exists to show: `Expiry (MM/YY)` above a `MM/YY` placeholder. # Composition Contract: how your code arranges Sando units This file is for the code you write beside installed Sando units: your screens, your own sections, and every call site where you place a Layout, a Component or a Block. It settles how units nest, how you lay them out across widths, what a call site looks like, how icons go in, and which parts of accessibility are yours to supply. How your own CSS is written is [`styling-contract.md`](styling-contract.md); which gap goes between two things is [`spacing-contract.md`](spacing-contract.md). Partially enforced: TypeScript refuses an icon-only `Button` without `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and any prop value outside its declared union. Nothing else in your repository checks this file. ## The four tiers Every Sando unit belongs to one of four tiers, and they compose downward only. | Tier | Owns | Examples | |---|---|---| | **Layout** | arrangement only: it positions whatever you pass it and renders no content of its own | `Stack`, `Grid`, `Container`, `LayoutGrid`, `AspectRatio`, `SplitLayout` | | **Component** | one primitive and its look; behaviour comes from React Aria | `Button`, `TextField`, `Card`, `Dialog`, `AppShell` | | **Block** | a reusable content section built from Components and Layouts | `LoginForm`, `StatCardGrid`, `Hero`, `DataTable` | | **Screen** | one specific page: chrome plus Blocks | your own pages | - **Your pages are Screens.** A Screen arranges Blocks, Layouts and Components. Nothing below it imports it. - **Never upward.** A section you write that two pages share is a Block-shaped unit of your own; it may use Components and Layouts, never a Screen. - **A Layout's `as` names structure, never a heading.** ``, `as="nav"`, `as="ul"` and `as="main"` are fine. `` is a heading drawn by hand, invisible to anything that counts headings: use `Text` with `elementType="h2"` instead. ## Where a Block sits: its posture Each Block is built for one of three postures, and the posture tells you what the parent has to supply. | Posture | What it is | Width | Heading | |---|---|---|---| | **Panel** (most Blocks) | dropped into a page next to sibling Blocks | full width: the parent (`Container`, `LayoutGrid`, a Frame) sets the cap | optional section label only, never a page title | | **Frame** | chrome that leaves its content region as an open `children` slot (`SidePanel`) | full width | none of its own | | **Self-contained** | the page itself, an overlay, or a standalone state | a span of the page grid that you set | may carry a default heading | So give a Panel its width from outside, and do not pass a Panel a page-title heading that your page's `PageHeader` already shows. The same postures apply to a section you build yourself: if it sits beside other sections, let the parent set its width. ## Arrange, never re-style You arrange units. You never reach into one to change how it looks. - **Need a unit to look different here? Use its props.** ` ``` (Sando installs into `src/layouts/`, `src/components/` and `src/blocks/`; the paths above are written from a file one level under `src/`, such as `src/pages/`.) - **`Container`** is a centred column that spans columns of the page grid (`span`, default 12, or `"full"`). It insets by the page margin unless it sits inside a frame that already does, where you pass `padding="none"`. Set `align="start"` for a form read down one column under a page title. - **`Stack`** is a one-direction flow: `direction` (`"column"` by default, or `"row"`), `gap`, `align`, `justify`, `wrap`, `grow`. - **`Grid`** is a two-direction grid: a fixed `columns` count, or `minItemWidth` for auto-fit columns that reflow by themselves. - **`LayoutGrid`** with `LayoutGridItem span` places regions on the page's column grid. - **A `Stack`'s `align` defaults to `stretch`, so a chip placed in a column comes out full width.** Set `align="start"` on the Stack when every child should hug its content, or give the chip a class of yours with `align-self: start` when a sibling must still fill. A `Button` or `Link` filling its column is normal; a stretched `Badge` or `Tag` is always a mistake. ## Responsive, mobile first Sando has one breakpoint ladder, the same in every theme: | Step | Applies from | |---|---| | `small` | the base value, every width | | `medium` | 768px and up | | `large` | 1024px and up | The step names are the size words, never `md`, `lg`, `mobile` or `desktop`. Reach for these three tools in order: 1. **Fluid Layouts first.** `Container` shrinks with its frame and `Grid minItemWidth` reflows its columns, so many screens need nothing more. 2. **Responsive props.** Every layout prop of `Stack`, `Grid`, `Container` and `LayoutGrid` accepts either one value or `{ small, medium, large }`. `small` is the base; an omitted step inherits the one below it. ```tsx ``` 3. **Your own `@media` block**, only for a structural change no prop expresses (a bar that turns into a menu button). Write `min-width: 768px` or `min-width: 1024px` and nothing else: never a `max-width` query, never a width of your own, and never `var()` inside the condition, because `@media` cannot read a custom property. The same widths apply to a `matchMedia` call. The larger space and radius steps already tighten on small screens, so a fixed `gap` adapts by itself. Use a responsive `gap` only when the relationship itself changes at a width, not to make it a little smaller. ## The shape of a call site - **Compound units are flat named exports from one file.** `Select` with `SelectItem`, `Tabs` with its parts: `import { Select, SelectItem } from "../components/Select"`, never `Select.Item`. - **There is no `asChild`.** Composition goes through `children`, React Aria's render props and its slots. - **`className` is added to the unit's own class, never in place of it.** Use it to give the unit a place in your arrangement (a grid area, an `align-self`), not to restyle it. - **`style` passes through and `ref` reaches the underlying DOM node** (a plain prop in React 19). - **`variant` names emphasis and intent, never a colour.** There is no `variant="brand"` or `variant="accent"`: the emphasis rungs are `primary`, `strong`, `tonal`, `secondary`, `outline`, `ghost`, `destructive`, `surface` and `link`. Status words are `success`, `warning`, `error` and `info`; `destructive` is an action, `error` is a status. - **`size` is `small`, `medium` or `large`**, and `medium` is what you get when you omit it. - **State props come from React Aria** (`isDisabled`, `isPending`, `isSelected`, ...). Pass them; never fake a state with a class. - **A Button with an icon and a word wraps the word in React Aria's `Text`**, so the label's optical inset lands on the text and not on the icon. A plain text label needs no wrapper. ```tsx import { Text } from "react-aria-components"; import { Plus } from "../components/icons"; ``` Use React Aria's `Text` here, not Sando's `Text` component: Sando's answers only a slot it is given by name. ## Icons at the call site 1. **Import icons from the installed `icons.tsx`, never from the icon library.** The library is a dependency of that module; your code uses the names it exports (`Plus`, `Search`, `Trash`, `Bell`, ...). An import from the library itself, or an inline `` (`alt=""` when the picture is decoration) | | 2.5.3 Label in name | the accessible name contains the words on screen | when you pass `aria-label` to a worded control, start it with the visible words | | 3.3.1 / 3.3.2 Errors and labels | every field is named and its errors are words | `label` on every field, `description` for instructions, `errorMessage` for the error; never a placeholder as the only label | | 4.1.3 Status messages | a change the user did not move focus to is announced | show it in an `Alert` or `Toast`, whose `live` prop (`"polite"` by default, `"assertive"` for what must interrupt) sets the announcement | Three more belong to the page you compose: - **Exactly one `h1` per screen.** It names the page, and every other heading on the screen sits below it in order (`h2` under it, `h3` under an `h2`). Promote the visible page title to it (``, or the unit that renders the page title). When the design shows no title (a home screen whose header is only a logo), the screen still owes one: render `

# Design language: your repository's design files

Every repository that builds a product on Sando keeps its design decisions in the same files, at the
same paths, so that any agent or designer who opens one knows where to look: what the service is and
how it treats its users, what each screen holds, which units it installs and how it composes them.
This page defines that layout, the order an agent reads it in when it builds a screen, what a screen
may do and where the rest of the service's code goes, and a template for each file.

Hand-maintained; no check reads this file.
